name: Q4 Practice (Descartes)
description: The same concepts tested on Quiz 4, rephrased with shuffled options so you practice the ideas without memorizing exact wording

questions.question: Which figure is credited with fusing Aristotle's philosophy with Roman Catholic Church doctrine to create Scholasticism?
options: St. Augustine
St. Thomas Aquinas
Emperor Constantine
Pope Gregory I

questions.question: What distinguishes Cartesian Doubt from ordinary Skepticism?
options: Cartesian Doubt leads to permanent uncertainty about the possibility of any knowledge
Cartesian Doubt is motivated by the desire to find an unshakeable foundation for knowledge
Cartesian Doubt was borrowed from the ancient Greek Skeptics like Pyrrho
Cartesian Doubt ultimately concludes that no reliable knowledge is possible

questions.question: Descartes' radical doubt leads him to conclude that all of the following can be doubted EXCEPT:
options: The reliability of his senses
Mathematical truths like 2 + 2 = 4
The fact that he exists as a thinking thing
The existence of the external physical world around him

questions.question: On which of the following points did Descartes actually agree with Aristotle?
options: That the universe is guided by a final purpose or Telos
That the soul gives life and animates the body
That the external physical world is a valid subject of scientific investigation
That forms are real and exist inside particular physical things

questions.question: The Wax Argument demonstrates all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Sensory experience of the wax changes completely as it melts
The mind grasps the identity of the wax through rational inspection rather than the senses
Our senses alone cannot identify the wax as the same object in both its solid and liquid form
The senses reliably pick out the primary qualities of the wax in both its states

questions.question: The Cogito ('I think, therefore I am') establishes all of the following EXCEPT:
options: That Descartes exists as a thinking thing
That the act of thinking is the one thing that cannot be doubted
That a direct proof of God's existence has been achieved through self-reflection
That existence requires the ongoing act of thinking to be confirmed

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Extended things (the physical world) according to Descartes?
options: They are three-dimensional and measurable in space
They are divisible into smaller and smaller parts
They are composed of an indivisible, immaterial substance
They follow the deterministic mechanical laws of nature

questions.question: Descartes' philosophy unintentionally gave rise to all of the following movements EXCEPT:
options: Modern Skepticism
Philosophical Idealism
Scientific Materialism
Medieval Scholasticism

questions.question: All of the following accurately describe the Problem of Interaction EXCEPT:
options: The mind is immaterial and the body is material, making direct causation difficult to explain
Descartes proposed the pineal gland as the site where mind-body interaction occurs
The Problem arises because two completely different types of substance must somehow communicate
The soul and body do not interact at all because they are entirely separate and never communicate

questions.question: According to Descartes, the human mind possesses all of the following EXCEPT:
options: The capacity for free will
The quality of being indivisible
Extension, meaning it occupies three-dimensional physical space
The ability to engage in rational thought and self-reflection

questions.question: The intellectual environment Descartes grew up in, fusing Aristotle's philosophy with Roman Catholic Church teachings, was called:
options: Platonism
Stoicism
Empiricism
Scholasticism

questions.question: Why is Descartes considered the unintentional father of Modern Skepticism?
options: He personally concluded in a later work that knowledge was ultimately impossible
Later philosophers accepted his method and Cogito but rejected his proofs of God and the external world
His followers deliberately misread the Meditations to support total philosophical uncertainty
He published a retraction arguing that the Cogito itself was too weak to resist radical doubt

questions.question: Which statement best captures Descartes' view on the relationship between the human mind and the laws of mechanics?
options: Both the mind and all matter are equally subject to the laws of mechanics
The mind is free from mechanical laws, while all matter in the universe obeys them completely
Mechanical laws govern the mind's connection to the body but not the soul's inner life
Neither the mind nor the body is truly subject to mechanical laws in Descartes' system

questions.question: The 'Cartesian Circle' describes which fatal flaw in Descartes' argument?
options: His proof of the Cogito relies on a circular self-referential claim
His proof of God depends on trusting innate ideas, but innate ideas are only trustworthy if God exists first
His argument for the external world loops back and only proves the mind's existence
His use of Scholastic premises to arrive at anti-Scholastic philosophical conclusions

questions.question: According to Descartes, what role does the soul play in the body's physical vitality and movement?
options: The soul animates the body like a pilot who steers and directs a ship from inside
The soul plays no role in animating the body; the body operates as a mechanical machine on its own
The soul controls the body through the flow of animal spirits in the nervous system and blood
The soul and body are so unified in humans that they cannot be meaningfully distinguished at all
